payload.claim: `_resolve_queue`'s own docstring says printing its result is the caller's job, and its sibling `_queue` discharges that by printing `resolved.reconciled`, `resolved.gh_failures` and `resolved.policy_unread` (see `_queue`, which calls `_print_reconcile_summary` and `_print_queue` with exactly those three). `_batch` calls `_resolve_queue` here but never reads `resolved.reconciled`, `resolved.gh_failures` or `resolved.policy_unread` anywhere in its body — an unattended night where `gh` could not run (so the open-PR/touches-overlap refusals never checked) or `policy.yaml` could not be read at `base_sha` (so the protected-path prefilter never ran) produces no stdout/event trace at all, unlike the attended path with the same underlying scan. The operator reading the morning log has no way to tell 'these checks never ran' from 'these checks ran and found nothing', which is precisely the ambiguity `_resolve_queue`'s own comment about `policy_unread` says must never be collapsed.
